documents.title: Sales tax collected, paid and what to remit
documents.content: The Sales Tax Calculator at /accounting/tax/sales-tax works out sales tax for a reporting period that starts as the current quarter. Tax Collected adds up the tax on income entries, Tax Paid adds up the tax on expense entries as input tax credits, and Net Tax Due is collected minus paid plus any amount carried forward that you type in. A negative result means you paid more tax than you collected. Entries are counted by their date as a plain day, so one dated on the first or last day of the period is included and one dated the day before or after is not. Entries marked Personal are never counted. Record Remittance Payment adds an expense to the ledger for the net amount, to Canada Revenue Agency, dated today, in the Taxes and Licenses category. It only works while the net is positive, the button is disabled while it saves so one click makes one entry, and the new entry shows in the page at once. It does not file anything with CRA, and it does not change the carried forward amount, so type the new balance in yourself.

documents.title: The Income Statement and tax categories
documents.content: The Tax Center at /accounting/tax links to the Income Statement, Manage Tax Categories, Manage Tax Rates, Capital Assets (CCA), the Sales Tax Calculator and Payroll Remittances. The Income Statement at /accounting/reports/income-statement follows the CRA T2125 layout: it adds up income entries for the chosen dates into sales and other income, groups expense entries by their tax line number, and shows net profit or loss. Quick buttons choose This Year or This Month. The dates are included on both ends, so 1 January is in the new year. Only business entries are included; entries marked Personal are left out. An expense whose category does not match a standard tax line is added to Other Expenses, so assign each entry to the right tax line, using Manage Tax Categories to add your own, for the statement to be accurate. The report reads the amounts as saved and is a summary to help you prepare, not a filed return.
